summary: Added build_evidence_insufficiency(...) and wired an always-present, JSON-serializable, deterministic `insufficiency` object into every verify_claim(...) response. It explains why a claim is not safely supported using only the conservative lexical signals verify_claim already computed (no semantic entailment / NLI / model use). All existing verify_claim keys and status/reasons behavior are unchanged (backward compatible); the object is additive.
implemented: build_evidence_insufficiency(status, items, evidence_map, conflict_evidence, claim_tokens, overlap, downgraded_by_conflict): returns {has_insufficiency, summary, blocking, missing_markers, conflict_count, overlap, details, method=deterministic_lexical_insufficiency_v1}. Deterministic and stdlib-only.
summary is a single stable label chosen by priority: no_retrieved_evidence > required_markers_missing > conflict_candidates_found > weak_lexical_overlap > none.

details is a list of machine-readable reason objects (each with a 'code'), not prose-only strings: no_retrieved_evidence, required_markers_missing (+markers), conflict_candidates_found (+conflict_count, conflict_types, downgraded_from_supported), weak_lexical_overlap (explicitly framed as lexical, not semantic).

verify_claim now computes the claim/evidence token overlap once (used by both the existing status logic and the insufficiency audit), tracks downgraded_by_conflict when a supported result is downgraded due to conflict candidates, and includes the `insufficiency` object in its return dict. All prior keys (claim, status, required_markers, missing_markers, cited_chunk_ids, evidence_map, conflict_evidence, reasons, search) are unchanged and still present.
HTTP POST /api/library/verify-claim naturally includes `insufficiency` via verify_claim (no handler change needed).

Added tests/test_claim_insufficiency.py: no-evidence, missing-marker (top-level + detail), conflict downgrade (conflict_count + blocking + downgraded_from_supported), supported/no-insufficiency, weak-lexical-overlap (lexical-not-semantic), helper determinism, and two HTTP tests (supported response includes insufficiency; no-evidence response is blocking).
